headline: Googlebook preorders open (Android+ChromeOS laptops from $899); Grok 4.7 ships; Kiel Staatskanzlei largely on Linux.

stories.title: Googlebook: Android+ChromeOS laptops open for preorder from $899
facts: Google blog (Sep 21): Googlebook — new laptop category on Android stack + ChromeOS desktop foundations, designed for Gemini Intelligence and Android phone pairing — preorders open today.
Hardware: Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo flagships; aluminum/magnesium/carbon; up to 2.8K OLED touch; Intel or Qualcomm + NPU >45 TOPS; up to ~14h battery; Glowbar returns on the lid.
Phone companion: Continue On, Files from phone, Cast My Apps; Gemini features include Magic Pointer, Rambler (speech→structured notes), Create My Widget.

Pricing/availability: from $899 with 12 months Google AI Pro (5TB + Gemini Advanced), 3 months YouTube Premium + Adobe Photoshop, up to 10 years of OS updates; shelves Oct 4 U.S. / Oct 5 CA, UK, IE, FR, DE, AU.
Security callout: ChromeOS-class stack with Titan root of trust plus a Level-5-certified pKVM Linux environment for agents/dev tools.
stories.whyItMatters: Google’s clearest premium-laptop bet since Chromebook — Android phone continuity plus Gemini on the desktop, with German retail on the Oct 5 wave.

image.alt: Googlebook laptop promotional image from Google’s product blog

stories.title: xAI ships Grok 4.7: longer coding runs, same $2/$6 pricing as 4.6
facts: xAI: Grok 4.7 is live — marketed as the most capable Grok for coding and knowledge work; longer hard-task runs, stricter self-checks, and “best-calibrated safeguards to date.”
Pricing matches Grok 4.6: $2 / $6 per million input/output tokens; a fast variant runs at twice the output speed for twice the price.
On CursorBench 4.0 (longer coding tasks), xAI charts Grok 4.7 at the price-performance frontier — e.g. Extra High 46.3% at ~$6.01 avg cost/task; High 43.9% / ~$4.69; Medium 41.6% / ~$3.49.
Larger base than 4.6 with a longer RL pass on multi-hour tasks; available today via the API, third-party coding harnesses, routers, and cloud platforms.
stories.whyItMatters: After weeks of delay chatter, the official model card/price finally landed — and the CursorBench framing is aimed squarely at agentic coding users.

stories.title: Kiel Staatskanzlei largely off Windows: 200+ staff on Linux
facts: heise: Schleswig-Holstein’s Staatskanzlei says the Windows→Linux switch is largely done — über 200 staff now on Linux; ~20 seats stay on Windows for Fachverfahren with no short-term alternative.
Digitalisierungsminister Dirk Schrödter (CDU) announced it Saturday at the 24. Kieler Open Source und Linux Tage; the chancellery is the pilot for a wider Landesverwaltung rollout now being planned.
Support: Dataport + Gonicus for Linux scale. Stack already includes LibreOffice, Open-Xchange, OpenTalk; next Nextcloud, Univention Nubus, telephony “Oskar.”
stories.whyItMatters: A concrete German Land milestone on digital sovereignty — not a press-slide plan, but production desktops in the government HQ.

image.alt: Illustration accompanying heise’s report on Kiel’s Linux migration

stories.title: ZuckOff: free app flags nearby Meta/Snap camera glasses over Bluetooth
facts: WIRED ME: Paweł Szydłowski’s free ZuckOff app listens for Bluetooth ads and flags Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta, and Snap Spectacles nearby; Pro adds background alerts/history/CSV.
It estimates rough proximity from signal strength but cannot tell if glasses are recording, who is wearing them, or guarantee silence means none are present (paired devices can go quiet).
HN (~298) boosted the story today; official site lists manufacturer signatures (e.g. Luxottica 0x0D53, Snap 0x03C2) and notes Android is still in a closed Play test.
stories.whyItMatters: A practical, single-dev counter to always-on camera glasses — limited, but one of the few tools that turns an invisible problem into a detectable one.
